How's your phosphorus level in your soil, compared to nitrogen? Beets need a healthy load of phosphorus to swell the roots. I grow two rows of beets, one where I've got lots of it and nitrogen for beet root, and one with high nitrogen just for greens.

It could also be the over wintering. I've had poor luck over wintering beets because they end up dumping all their energy saved in fall into seeding early in spring. Usually results in what you described, super sweet but incredibly small woody roots.

Don't have the money to be spending $40 on soil tests for every single area in my garden, and I'm probably moving next year and won't have any room to grow anything at all anymore anyway. But I don't use high nitrogen fertilizer in that bed.

The thing is beets never grow to an appropriate size in my area if you plant them in early spring or late summer. So the only option is to overwinter.
